To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we introduced a novel task for discovering ongoing conversations in dialog blocks; (b) we introduced a publicly available test bed for the task by surrogating personal dialogs with theatrical plays; and (c) we showed that language use shift features and script features are important in modeling this task.

(1) the task of finding threads in scattered dialog blocks is challenging, (2) the task is solvable with syntactic and semantic information, (3) the best results are obtained with models that use features capturing shifts in the language use, and (4) the best results, so far, are obtained with models based on a combination of syntactic, semantic and script features.

(1) the proposed testbed is useful for studying ongoing conversations in scattered dialogs; (2) the task can be solved with syntactic and semantic models, and (3) models should capture shifts in language use.

the following: (i) how to surmount the privacy problem in Big Personal Data; (ii) how to discover conversations in scattered dialog data; and (iii) what features and learning models should we use for this task.
